html:
The sophists were travelling teachers in Greece in the 5th and 4th centuries BCE who taught for a fee, above all the art of speaking well. Their students were mostly young men from rich families who wanted to succeed in public life.

Athenian democracy made them valuable. Citizens argued their own cases in court and spoke in the Assembly, so the ability to persuade meant power. Famous sophists included:

  • Protagoras of Abdera, who said "man is the measure of all things"
  • Gorgias of Leontini, who dazzled Athens with his style when he came as an envoy in 427 BCE
  • Prodicus and Hippias, who taught language, history and science

Many Athenians distrusted them. Critics said they taught people to win arguments rather than find the truth, and to make the weaker case look the stronger. Aristophanes mocked them in The Clouds and lumped Socrates in with them, though Socrates took no fees. Plato wrote against them, and our word "sophistry" comes from his picture of them.
sum: The sophists were travelling teachers in Greece in the 5th and 4th centuries BCE who taught for a fee, above all the art of speaking well. Their students were mostly young men from rich families who wanted to succeed in public life.
